newsitem.title: UK: Investors stick with Algeria despite violence.
newsitem.headline: Investors stick with Algeria despite violence.

text.p: The latest surge in violence in oil and gas rich Algeria has so far failed to put off foreign investors but analysts on Tuesday warned that it may be time for some to sell and take their profits.

"The political risk is being discounted. The oil revenue behind them is huge and their (debt) repayment schedule looks comfortable even when the price is down to $19 a barrel," Indosuez analyst Bradley Wickens said.
More than 150 people have been killed in a wave of attacks by Islamic rebels since the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan on January 10.
The lader of Algeria's Armed Islamic Group threatened to step up attacks in its campaign against the secular military-backed government.
Despite the attacks, the country's rescheduled commercial debt -- worth more than $3 billion -- has risen sharply on the emerging debt market.
Since last August, debt prices have jumped more than 40 percent and in the past two weeks rallied again, partly on the general interest in high yield paper offered by emerging countries.
Tranche A paper -- the most liquid of Algeria's commercial debt on the secondary market -- is now fetching around 84 cents in the dollar, compared to only 59 cents in August.

"The government has been able to protect economically significant areas from this violence...but there's always the risk that the terrorists will begin to focus on economic targets," Salomon Brothers emerging markets analyst David Boren said.
Wickens said though investors had become somewhat blase to the violence, it would be quite a different matter if Islamic fundamentals did come to power.
"At the moment people are seeing oil and dollar signs. I'd sell at these levels and profit-take," he added.
However, as long as the oil and gas fields are protected from attacks, analysts said Algeria was expected to keep its economy on track and stick to its programme with the International Monetary Fund.
